title: Per-token flexible bands for heavy-tail streaming usage — pricing probe
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: A subset of customers generate long-running streaming sessions or heavy tail output (long completion outputs) that drive disproportionate egress costs and latency risk. Existing per-token pricing with static input/output rates and flat streaming minimums produces two problems: (1) it under-prices very short interactive sessions while overcharging bursty long outputs, and (2) it creates unpredictability for enterprise contracts that must reconcile commit floors with bursts. Goal: Design a controlled experiment that evaluates 'flex bands' — a small set of per-token rate bands and session-aware grace logic that dynamically adjusts per-token unit pricing for streaming sessions with heavy-output tails. We want to measure revenue, friction, accuracy of customer bill predictions, and legal/SQ impacts for enterprise contract language. Hypothesis: Introducing flexible bands (3 price bands based on recent output-token distribution per session: short, medium, long) with a lightweight grace window (first N tokens billed at band X then fallback) will (a) smooth revenue variance across customers, (b) reduce wholesale refunds/charge disputes from power users, and (c preserve developer-facing simplicity when surfaced via SDK defaults. Experiment design:
- Identify cohort: customers in last 90 days with >95th percentile session outputs (by tokens) and a control cohort matched by ARR and vertical.
- Variants: Control (current billing); Variant A (3 bands for output: short <=256, medium 257-2048, long >2048 with stepped per-token rates); Variant B (same bands + session-grace: first 512 tokens billed at medium band for sessions that spike unexpectedly).
- Metrics (primary/secondary): Primary: delta in net revenue per customer, frequency of billing disputes, number of refunds. Secondary: latency P95 for streaming, % of sessions hitting long band, change in avg cost-per-1k tokens for customers.
- Data sources: token telemetry (ingress/egress), streaming session logs, billing records, support tickets tagged "billing-dispute", contract commit telemetry.
- Duration: 6 weeks (2 week ramp, 4 week measurement).
- Segmentation: enterprise vs self-serve; on/off for enterprise commit customers (flagged) to include a contract-protection mode.
Enterprise SQ & contract work: Draft recommended contract language for commits and minimums that explains flex bands and grace windows. Coordinate with Legal to update enterprise playbooks and with Finance for invoicing templates. Security questionnaire implications: document how billing events and token-level telemetry are stored and accessible for audits; confirm that token metrics disclosed to customers are derived aggregates (no raw prompt/response dumps). Implementation tasks: API/SDK surface: add billing-band header and pricing metadata endpoint for customers to preview projected band for a session; Console: add per-session band histogram and projected billing preview in session trace. Backend: billing pipeline change to assign band at finalization time, add rate table and fallback logic. Acceptance criteria: low false-positive band assignments (<1%), <2% lift in latency P95, legal sign-off on contract language, finance confirms invoiceability, internal docs and customer FAQ updated. Rollout plan: small enterprise pilot (5 customers) -> broader A/B to 10% of accounts -> full opt-in for new customers -> default change 30 days after publishing clear migration guidance. Risks & mitigations:
- Customer confusion: provide transparent pre-bill previews in Console and SDK; run webinars and outbound comms.
- Revenue leakage: use conservative band pricing and monitor daily revenue delta.
- Contract disputes: require opt-in for contracted customers unless legal-approved amendment. Deliverables: PRD, experiment dashboard, SDK patch, contract language draft, support playbook, postmortem with recommended permanent pricing model. Timeline: PRD + legal draft by 2025-02-20; infra spike and SDK changes by 2025-03-07; pilot start 2025-03-17; pilot end 2025-04-14; decision milestone 2025-04-30.
acceptance_criteria: Experimented variants instrumented and gated behind flags
Daily revenue delta dashboard available and validated
Legal and Finance sign-off on enterprise contract addendum
Console/session preview shows projected billing before finalization
Latency P95 impact < 2% and band assignment false positives < 1%
